html:
The Secotan were an Algonquian people of the coastal sounds of North Carolina, between Albemarle and Pamlico sounds, with villages such as Secotan, Aquascogoc, Pomeiooc and Roanoac. They farmed maize and fished with weirs.

They were the people the English met during the Roanoke voyages of 1584 to 1590. The artist John White painted their villages, fields and people; his watercolours are the best early images of Indigenous North Americans. Relations went bad quickly: in 1586 the colonists under Ralph Lane killed their leader Wingina. Their neighbours were the Chowanoke, Pamlico and Weapemeoc; see also Roanoke.
